Payroll clearing reconciliation

Finds what is stuck in the payroll clearing account and why, tests each payroll liability for the balance it should carry, and proposes entries for a person to post.

Watch someone use it

Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, payroll clearing 2200 and the payroll liabilities, September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

Claudewith the MosoFin payroll clearing reconciliation skill

Our payroll clearing account never gets back to zero. Can you reconcile it for September?

Claude

Yes. Before I read anything, I need eight answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.

  1. Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload files?
  2. Which company? I propose the payroll accounts from your chart, and you confirm them.
  3. Which period?
  4. How often do you pay each liability: monthly, semi-weekly or quarterly? I never assume this.
  5. Please attach the payroll register for the period.
  6. Please attach the bank statement for the period.
  7. Up to what amount may I propose a write-off, and who approves it?
  8. Do you have a statement of account from the tax authority or a benefit provider?

Use MosoFin. Northbrook Trading, September. Federal taxes monthly by the 15th, 401(k) monthly by the 7th, state unemployment quarterly. Register and bank statement attached. Write-offs under $50, and I approve them. No statements of account.

Claude

Here is my plan. I reconcile 2200 Payroll clearing, 2210 Federal payroll taxes, 2230 401(k) and 2240 State unemployment for September. No payroll platform is connected, so your register gives the accrued side. Federal taxes and 401(k) are paid monthly, and state unemployment quarterly. I read twelve months of detail, from 1 October 2025, and tie net pay to your bank statement. Shall I start?

Yes, go ahead.

Claude

One check on scope first. 2250 Accrued payroll also has payroll entries, $2,500 at 30 September. It is not on your list. Do you want me to include it?

No. I review 2250 with the month-end accruals.

Claude

I list 2250 as excluded, with your reason. Now 2200. September's two pay runs each net to nil in 2200. So 2200 should hold nil, but it holds $4,023.40. Five items are stuck in it:

2200 Payroll clearing at 30 Sep
ItemAmountIn 2200 sinceDays
Old balance, no detail in the twelve months$23.40before 1 Oct 2025over 364
EE-03, direct deposit returned, not paid again$640.00Tue 3 Feb239
EE-05, final pay held in a dispute$1,150.00Thu 30 Apr153
EE-11, check #1987 not cashed, voided$410.00Tue 30 Jun92
JE-0912, memo “reclass contractor”, no pay run$1,800.00Thu 24 Sep6

Four items, $2,223.40, are more than 60 days old. The oldest is from before October 2025. Only $23.40 never cleared at any time in the twelve months. JE-0912 debits 6000 Wages, but no pay run is behind it. I show staff by reference only, never by name.

Claude

2210 looks fine at first. Its roll-forward ties to the books. But you pay monthly, so at a month end it should hold one month of taxes:

2210 Federal payroll taxes
GL balance at 30 Sep$27,000.00
− September taxes, due Thu 15 Oct$14,400.00
= August taxes, not paid$12,600.00

The August deposit was due on Tue 15 Sep. Part of it is tax that you withheld from your staff. A person who willfully does not pay that can be personally liable. It needs a payment, not an entry.

Claude

The money that did leave ties to the bank:

Bank and deposit ties
CheckAmountResult
Net pay, register against the bank statement$40,800.00Ties
401(k) for August, paid Fri 4 Sep, due Mon 7 Sep$3,400.00Ties
Federal taxes for August, due Tue 15 Sep$12,600.00Not paid

The year-to-date test on 2210 also ties: 12,300 + 116,100 − 101,400 = 27,000. It uses the same closing balance, so it cannot show the unpaid August. Only your monthly cadence shows it.

Can you write the whole $4,023.40 off to miscellaneous expense, so 2200 is clean?

Claude

No. $1,050 of it is pay that two people did not get. You still owe it to them. I propose these entries instead:

Proposals
ItemAmountProposal
P1 · EE-03 and EE-11$1,050.00Dr 2200, Cr 2260 Unclaimed wages payable
P2 · Old balance$23.40Dr 2200, Cr 7900 Other income, under your $50
P3 · JE-0912$1,800.00Dr 2200, Cr 2000 Accounts payable, if it is a contractor's bill
EE-05$1,150.00No entry until the dispute ends
2210 · August$12,600.00A payment for you to make
2210 · September$14,400.00Timing, due Thu 15 Oct, no entry
2240 · below zero−$150.00A refund to claim. Get the state's statement first

After P1, P2 and P3, 2200 holds $1,150, the disputed final pay. P2 holds only if the older detail names no person. Your state's rules decide when unclaimed pay goes to the state. A person posts these entries. I do not.

Claude

Your workpaper has a tab for each account, the summary, the bank tie-out, the proposed entries, the stale balances and the coverage.
